blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Higher electricity rates and more power outages may be suffered by the country as the super El Niño threatens to strain the energy system and trigger a surge in consumption, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said on Tuesday. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) earlier, a state of calamity has been declared in 106 cities and municipalities in the country, affecting 388,000 people, due to the effects of the weather phenomenon. Even without El Niño, Filipinos are already airing their frustrations over elevated power costs, triggered by surging oil prices following renewed tensions in […]...
